Acceptance criteria.d: The conditions a user story must meet to be accepted as done, usually written by the product owner. Testers turn them into test cases.

Accessibility tree.d: The browser's structured description of a page (headings, buttons, text boxes and their names) used by screen readers. Playwright MCP reads it to understand pages without screenshots.

API token.d: A long secret string that lets a program sign in to a service (such as Jira) on your behalf instead of a password. Treat it like a password and keep it out of code and chats.

Headless browser.d: A web browser running without a visible window, controlled by software. Used for automated tests and on servers with no screen.

JQL.d: Jira Query Language: Jira's search language, for example: project = PAY AND issuetype = Bug AND status != Done.

Least privilege.d: The security principle of giving a person, program or AI only the access it needs for its task, and nothing more.

Locator.d: In Playwright, a way of finding an element on the page, ideally the way a user would (by role, label or text) rather than by fragile CSS details.

OAuth.d: A standard way to let an app act on your behalf without giving it your password: you sign in on the service's own page and approve, and the app receives a revocable access token.

Playwright.d: A free, open-source tool from Microsoft for automating Chromium, Firefox and WebKit browsers, widely used for end-to-end testing.

Storage state.d: A saved file of a browser's cookies and local storage, used to start automated sessions already logged in.
